claims.statement: The enclosing context is unsupported in a composite action's run keyword and should be referenced via env. This fragment does not identify the context; do not generalize to every context.
Larger-runner Capacity settings use Maximum concurrency to bound simultaneous jobs, then Save; target capacity, costs and effective autoscaling are not observed.

Job and service containers on the same user-defined Docker bridge expose ports to each other without host port mapping; workflow service label provides access. This is container-local networking, not universal host reachability or port-isolation proof.
Contexts, objects and properties vary with workflow run conditions; absent properties must not be assumed to be present from an example.
Shown context is only an example whose content depends on its workflow; shared context-contents dependency reinforces variability and needs separate rendering resolution.

Workflow/action authors should evaluate execution of attacker-controlled input; certain contexts are untrusted because malicious content can be inserted. Linked script-injection mitigation is not implicitly reviewed.
Copying a runner label through More options and Copy label is optional workflow authoring assistance, not permission to use the runner or a verified assignment.
The enclosing workflow may be copied into .github/workflows and adapted; source copying is not license clearance, execution safety or authorization to deploy.

Azure App Service plan example uses az appservice plan create with existing resource-group and new-plan placeholders and --is-linux; Azure authentication/resource-group references remain separate. No account login, billable provisioning or command execution occurs.

Deployment tutorial generates a publish profile and stores its full contents in repository secret AZURE_WEBAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE. These are credential-bearing operations requiring separate authority; no credentials generated, retrieved, exposed or written.
Create group applies the previously chosen policy in the parent procedure; this UI step alone proves neither authorized scope nor actual enforced access.
Enterprise-group documentation authoring comment requires a contextual self-hosted or larger-runner security admonition; comment is source evidence, not executable instruction.

Enterprise runner groups may restrict organizations and conditionally workflows in GHEC/GHES; organization owners add granular repository/conditional workflow policies. Unspecified registration group means default group, later movable; creation requires choosing organizational access policy.
Enterprise creation uses separate first-step, organization-access and workflow-policy includes then Save group. Included contents and native enforcement are not implied by standalone review.

Organization creation comment requires a contextual runner security admonition. Creation chooses allowed repositories and GHEC/GHES workflows; organization owners and conditionally custom-role users with Manage organization runners and runner groups may manage policy.

Every organization has one default group; additional FPT groups require Team organization owners, while other branches permit owners and conditionally authorized custom-role users. Registration without a group uses default; moving and REST creation are referenced.

Procedure navigates organization settings, creates/names a group and includes repository/workflow policy assignment. In GHEC/GHES, organization-owned groups cannot access another organization's workflows; enterprise-owned group is required. Linked/includes remain separate.
Custom deployment rules are described for public repositories on all plans, but private/internal requires Enterprise; gated-feature include and exact current eligibility remain separately verified.
Pinned custom deployment protection is public preview and subject to change, not current feature availability certification.
Any number of GitHub-App-based protection rules can be installed on a repository, but at most six may be enabled simultaneously per environment. Installed quantity is not enforcement coverage.
For same-name default settings, the most specific wins; job default overrides workflow default. This describes defaults, not every unrelated configuration precedence rule.

Tutorial substitutes the configured environment name, otherwise removes environment; FPT/GHEC also directs removal for private repositories without GHE Cloud. This source branch is not authority to remove deployment protections or bypass unavailable capabilities.

Dependabot can keep action and reusable-workflow references updated; source describes bug-fix/features benefits and automatic maintenance, not proof that updates are tested, safe, accepted or merged. Linked procedures and security-updates behavior remain separate.

Enterprise/organization owners in GHEC/GHES, or organization owners in FPT, may select repositories allowed to create repository-level self-hosted runners. Conditional custom-role permission is limited to repositories within that organization; enterprise and organization policy links require separate review.
